relations.subject: Hu Shih
relations.evidence: On 16 August 1910, he was sent to study agriculture at Cornell University in the United States. In 1912, he changed his major to philosophy and literature

relations.subject: Hu Shih
relations.evidence: After receiving his undergraduate degree, he went to study philosophy at Teachers College, Columbia University, in New York City

relations.subject: Hu Shih
relations.evidence: where he was influenced by his professor, John Dewey, and started literary experiments.

relations.subject: Hu Shih
relations.evidence: Hu returned to lecture in Peking University.

relations.subject: Wen Yuan-ning
relations.evidence: His Peking University colleague Wen Yuan-ning dubbed Hu a Philosophe for his humanistic interests and expertise.

relations.subject: Chien-Shiung Wu
relations.evidence: At the university Hu became a well-liked professor, whose top students included award-winning physicist Chien-Shiung Wu.

relations.subject: Hu Shih
relations.evidence: Hu then served as chancellor of Peking University, at the time called National Peking University, between 1946 and 1948.

relations.subject: Hu Shih
relations.evidence: In 1957, he became the third president of the Academia Sinica in Taipei, a post he retained until his death.

relations.subject: Hu Shih
relations.evidence: In his essay "Introducing My Thoughts" (介紹我自己的思想), he states that Thomas H. Huxley is the one person who most heavily influenced his thoughts.

relations.subject: Cai Yuanpei
relations.evidence: Cai Yuanpei, president of Peking University where Hu was teaching at the time, wrote the preface for Outline
